# Herdr Obsidian Vault

<a href="https://miguelalexanderdiaz.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/"><img src="docs/assets/docs-button.svg" alt="Read the documentation" width="196" height="44"></a>

Browse an [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) vault from a side panel in the [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) desktop app, and read its notes in a floating window that draws them the way Obsidian does. Read-only: it never writes into your vault.

![Schematic of the Vault panel on the left and the floating Vault reader on the right. A drawing, not a screenshot.](docs/assets/layout.svg)

*The picture above is a schematic of the layout, not a screenshot.*

Two Herdr mods live in this repository:

| Mod | Folder | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vault` | `mods/vault` | The panel: a vault picker fed by Obsidian's own vault list, a file tree, and full-text search with ripgrep. |
| `vault-reader` | `mods/vault-reader` | The floating reader: front matter, callouts, wikilinks, embeds, images, tasks, tags, tables, math, Mermaid, Excalidraw, Canvas and PDFs. |

Install both, under these exact names. A sample vault to try them on is in `examples/sample-vault`.

Documentation for people and agents: [docs site](docs/index.html) (GitHub Pages from `/docs`), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [llms.txt](llms.txt), [RECIPE.md](RECIPE.md), [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Support level

macOS is the only OS the author uses; Linux and Windows code paths are implemented and covered by fake-platform unit tests but not run in the live app.

The mods look for every external program in the places used by macOS, Linux and Windows, and say in the panel which one is missing. Reports from Linux and Windows are welcome: [docs/verify.html](docs/verify.html) is a short checklist on the sample vault with a report template.

A CI workflow template is in `scripts/ci.workflow.yml`. It has not run yet because the author still has to install it, so no system is claimed to be checked by it.

## Install

Both ways need the Herdr desktop app. Read [what the mods read, run and download](#privacy) first.

### One command

macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/main/install/install.sh | sh
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/main/install/install.ps1 | iex
```

It says what the mods reach (remote pictures in notes, the programs they run, what they read) and asks before writing anything. Then it copies `mods/vault` and `mods/vault-reader` into your Herdr home, adds `ctrl-shift-m` to `keys.json` (asking before it replaces a key you use) and runs `herdr-app check`. The portrait layout's installer adds the Vault panel when it finds these mods. Anything it replaces is backed up first under `community/herdr-obsidian-vault/` in the Herdr home;
running it again updates in place. From a clone: `install/install.sh` (or `.\install\install.ps1`).
No questions: `sh -s -- --yes` (Windows: `$env:HERDR_YES = 1` first). Another Herdr home: `--home
<folder>` or `HERDR_APP_HOME`. Merging `keys.json` uses Node, or on macOS the system's own JavaScript;
without either it prints the keys to add by hand.

### With a Herdr agent

Paste this to an agent running in Herdr, with the repository address filled in:

```text
Install the Herdr mods from https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault .
It has two mods, mods/vault and mods/vault-reader, and a keys.json.
Read every file first, tell me what they run and fetch, copy both
folders into my mods folder without overwriting anything, merge
keys.json after asking me about clashes, run herdr-app check on both
mods, then add the Vault panel to my layout.
```

### By hand

1. Clone or download this repository.
2. Find your Herdr home: `herdr-app --help` ends with a line `Home: ~/.config/herdr-app (HERDR_APP_HOME picks another)`. Here `~` is your user folder; the default is `.config/herdr-app` inside it, unless `HERDR_APP_HOME` is set. This default is quoted from Herdr's help and has not been checked on Windows. Copy `mods/vault` and `mods/vault-reader` into the `mods` folder of that home. Do not overwrite a mod of the same name; rename instead (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#renaming-a-mod)).

   ```sh
   # macOS and Linux
   cp -R mods/vault mods/vault-reader ~/.config/herdr-app/mods/
   ```

   ```powershell
   # Windows PowerShell: $env:HERDR_APP_HOME if set, else the default under your user folder
   $h = if ($env:HERDR_APP_HOME) { $env:HERDR_APP_HOME } else { "$HOME\.config\herdr-app" }
   Copy-Item -Recurse mods\vault, mods\vault-reader "$h\mods"
   ```

3. Merge the optional key of `keys.json` (Ctrl+Shift+M opens the panel as a popup) into your own `keys.json`.
4. Check both mods. Both must pass; Herdr reloads mods on its own, there is no restart.

   ```sh
   herdr-app check ~/.config/herdr-app/mods/vault
   herdr-app check ~/.config/herdr-app/mods/vault-reader
   ```

### Show the panel

The mods are installed with `"place": "none"`, so nothing shows until you place the panel. Add a block to a column or stack in a layout file:

```json
{ "id": "vault", "type": "block", "content": { "mod": "vault" } }
```

For the portrait layout (`herdr-portrait-layout`), append it to the children of the node with id `panel-body`; its bar then shows a Vault button by itself. You can also split a pane with the app command `pane.split` and `mod` set to `vault`, or skip the layout: the optional key Ctrl+Shift+M in `keys.json` opens the panel as a 420 by 640 popup. See the [install page](docs/install.html) for more.

On first run the panel lists the vaults Obsidian already knows. Otherwise use **Add vault** and pick a folder that contains `.obsidian`.

## Use

- Click a note, canvas, drawing, image or PDF in the tree to open it in the reader. Other files open with your system.
- Type two letters or more in the search box. Up and Down move, Enter opens, Esc clears.
- In the reader: Esc closes, Alt+Left or Backspace (and Cmd+[ on macOS) goes back, links open notes in place, **Web images: on/off** controls downloads, and **Keep** pins a note into a tab named `obsidian`.

Details are on the [usage page](docs/usage.html). Notes over 1 MiB cannot be opened in the reader, an opened PDF shows its first 30 pages, and nothing is editable; the [limits](docs/usage.html#limits) list the rest.

## Requirements

Only Herdr is required. Each program below adds a feature; without it you get a plain message, not a failure. Programs are found on PATH and then in the usual install folders of each system. Vaults must be inside your home folder.

| Program | Used for | Without it | macOS | Linux | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Herdr desktop app | Runs both mods. | Nothing works. | Install Herdr. | Install Herdr. | Install Herdr. |
| ripgrep (`rg`) | The search box in the Vault panel. | Search shows `ripgrep (rg) isn't installed:` and the install hint for your system. Browsing and reading still work. | `brew install ripgrep` | install ripgrep with your package manager (for example: `apt install ripgrep`) | `winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC` |
| Node.js 22.4 or newer (`node`) | Drawing math, Mermaid diagrams and Excalidraw drawings (the render script). | One line above the note names what is missing; the source of each diagram, formula or drawing stays visible. | `brew install node` | install Node.js 22.4 or newer (nodejs.org, or your package manager) | `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS` |
| A Chromium-family browser (Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave) | Runs headless to take a picture of each diagram, formula and drawing. | Same: one line above the note, `A Chromium-based browser wasn't found`, and the source stays visible. | Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`) | Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge in `/usr/bin`, `/opt` or `/snap/bin`, or on PATH (Flatpak browsers are not looked for) | Edge, Chrome or Brave in Program Files or Local AppData (Edge is built into Windows) |
| Obsidian desktop app | Supplies its own Mermaid and MathJax, read at run time from `obsidian.asar`. | Same: one line above the note, `The Obsidian app wasn't found`, and the source stays visible. Notes, canvases and images still open. | Obsidian in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`) | Obsidian from `/opt`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/share`, Snap or Flatpak (an AppImage cannot be found: name its file in `settings.json`) | Obsidian in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` or Program Files |
| Poppler (`pdftoppm`, `pdfinfo`) | Every page of a PDF (the first 30). | macOS draws page 1 through Quick Look. Linux and Windows show `Poppler (pdftoppm, pdfinfo) isn't installed:` with the hint, and the PDF opens in your default app. | `brew install poppler` | install poppler-utils with your package manager (for example: `apt install poppler-utils`) | `scoop install poppler` |
| curl | Downloading web images that a note shows with `![](https://...)`. | Those images show `curl isn't installed:` with the hint. Turn web images off on purpose with the Web images button. | Ships with macOS | install curl with your package manager (for example: `apt install curl`) | Ships with Windows 10 and newer |
| System file opener | Opening files the reader cannot show, web links, and PDFs in your viewer. | The click does nothing. | `open` (built in) | `xdg-open` (package `xdg-utils`) | `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` (built in) |

To install the optional programs in one go (the same commands as the table; a missing one is only a feature lost):

```sh
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install ripgrep node poppler
# Linux (Debian and Ubuntu names; use your package manager's)
sudo apt install ripgrep poppler-utils curl
```

```powershell
# Windows
winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC OpenJS.NodeJS
scoop install poppler
```

A browser or Obsidian in an unusual place: add `"browser"` and `"asar"` (absolute paths) to `data/vault/settings.json` in the Herdr home, no restart needed. The environment variables `HERDR_VAULT_BROWSER` (or `CHROME_PATH`) and `HERDR_VAULT_ASAR` also work, but only if Herdr itself was started with them. The search order and where Obsidian keeps its vault list on each system are on the [requirements page](docs/requirements.html).

## Privacy

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Reads | the selected vault folder (the render script also reads the pictures that an Excalidraw drawing embeds), Obsidian's vault list (on first run and on Import), and Obsidian's `obsidian.asar` (only Mermaid and MathJax) |
| Runs | `rg`, `node`, a headless Chromium-family browser (with a loopback-only debugging port for one render run), `pdfinfo`, `pdftoppm`, `curl`, the system opener (`open`, `xdg-open`, `rundll32`), `stat` or PowerShell for file timestamps, your login shell or `where` to find a program, and on macOS `qlmanage` and `sips` as fallbacks |
| Downloads | web images that a note shows, with `curl`; switch off with the **Web images** button (setting `remoteImages`) |
| Writes | only `data/vault` in the Herdr home: picture cache, Mermaid and MathJax copies, a temporary browser profile per render, settings. Herdr's own `shared.json` keeps vault paths after uninstall ([how to clear them](docs/install.html#uninstall)) |
| Never | writes into the vault, sends note text anywhere, runs Dataview or other plugin code, opens `file:` or `obsidian:` links, launches programs from a note |

The full list is on the [privacy page](docs/privacy.html).

## Troubleshooting

- **Search says `ripgrep (rg) isn't installed`**: install `rg` (table above).
- **Diagrams or formulas show their source**: Node.js 22.4+, a Chromium-family browser or the Obsidian app is missing; one line above the note names it.
- **A PDF shows one page or an install hint**: install Poppler.
- **The vault is listed dimmed, or not at all**: it must be inside your home folder; use Add vault or Import from Obsidian.
- **A web image is missing**: check the Web images button and that `curl` exists.
- **Wipe the cache**: delete `data/vault/cache` in the Herdr home.

The [troubleshooting page](docs/troubleshooting.html) has every message with its fix.

## Uninstall

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/main/install/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
```

(Windows: `$env:HERDR_UNINSTALL = 1` before the `irm ... | iex` line.) It removes what it installed
and the keys it added (not ones you changed since), backing them up first. It leaves `data/vault`, the cache and settings, in place.

By hand: Remove the block from your layout and the keys you merged, delete `mods/vault` and `mods/vault-reader` from your Herdr home, and optionally delete `data/vault` there. Your vaults are never touched.

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI agents that install, adapt, test or edit this repository. People should read [README.md](README.md) first. A short machine-readable map is in [llms.txt](llms.txt).

## What this repository is

Two Herdr desktop-app mods that let a person browse and read an Obsidian vault:

- `mods/vault`: the panel. Vault picker, file tree, ripgrep search. Opens notes in the reader.
- `mods/vault-reader`: the floating reader. Draws a note: properties, callouts, wikilinks, embeds, images, PDFs, math, Mermaid, Excalidraw, Canvas.

Both are read-only toward the vault. They are installed together, under exactly these folder names.

Herdr mods are JavaScript that describes native GPUI elements (gpui-kit). There is no DOM and no Node API inside a mod. The truth about the API is in the Herdr home folder: `AGENTS.md`, `herdr.d.ts` and `gpui-kit.d.ts` (Herdr rewrites the type files on every start). The home is `~/.config/herdr-app` unless `HERDR_APP_HOME` says otherwise; `herdr-app --help` prints it.

## File map

| Path | What | Runs in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mods/vault/main.js` | panel view, vault list, tree, add vault, picker menu | Herdr (mod) |
| `mods/vault/search.js`, `search-core.js` | ripgrep search glue, and the pure logic (arguments, parsing, ranking, snippet) | Herdr / plain Node |
| `mods/vault/obsidian-config.js`, `tree.js` | Obsidian's vault list parser, tree rules | Herdr and plain Node |
| `mods/vault-reader/main.js` | reader view, loading, links, Keep menu, keys | Herdr (mod) |
| `mods/vault-reader/parse.js`, `doc.js`, `canvas.js` | pure functions: Markdown to blocks, file to document, canvas to cards | Herdr and plain Node |
| `mods/vault-reader/assets.js`, `assets-core.js`, `vault-files.js` | pictures (images, PDF pages, web images, render jobs, cache) and the vault file walk: glue in Herdr, logic without Herdr imports | Herdr / plain Node |
| `mods/*/watch.js`, `mods/*/mod-name.js` | restartable folder watcher with timer fallback (identical in both mods); the mod folder name constants | Herdr and plain Node |
| `mods/*/platform.js` | every operating-system specific literal: tool lookup, install hints, openers, config paths, file stamps, image headers | Herdr and plain Node |
| `mods/vault-reader/render/` | `render.mjs`, `lib.mjs` and `browser.mjs` (plain Node: the script, its helpers, and the browser process of one run), `page.html`, `page.js`, `excalidraw.js`, `lzstring.js` (browser) | Node and the headless browser |
| `mods/*/mod.json`, `mods/*/icons/` | mod manifest, Lucide icons | Herdr |
| `examples/sample-vault/` | test vault: one file per feature | tests and manual checks |
| `tests/` | `npm test` suite, `fixtures/`, `stubs/` (strict stand-ins for Herdr's modules), `tools/` | plain Node |
| `docs/` | the GitHub Pages site (plain HTML and CSS) | browsers |
| `scripts/` | `check-docs.mjs`, `check-repo.mjs`, `check-recipe.mjs`, `privacy-scan.mjs`, `syntax-check.mjs`, `install-sim.mjs`, `typecheck.mjs`, `build-llms-full.mjs`, `doc-claims.json`, `ci.workflow.yml` (CI template), publish checklists | plain Node |
| `RECIPE.md`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSE`, `keys.json` | brief to rebuild, third-party credits, license, optional keys | |

## Tell the person before you install

Herdr's rule is to tell the person first when a mod reaches the network, runs programs or reads outside its own folder. This one does all three. Say, in your own words:

- **Reads**: the folder of the selected vault (recursively, with a watcher), Obsidian's vault list (`obsidian.json` in Obsidian's config folder; on first run and again on every **Import from Obsidian**), and, for diagrams and math, Obsidian's `obsidian.asar` (only its Mermaid and MathJax files). The render script (`node`) also reads, with Node's own file access, the picture files that an Excalidraw drawing embeds by reference from the vault.
- **Runs** (none bundled): `rg`, `node`, a headless Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave (with a loopback-only DevTools port for the length of one render run, and a page served from `127.0.0.1`), `pdfinfo` and `pdftoppm`, `curl`, the system opener (`open`, `xdg-open`, `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`), `stat` (macOS, Linux) or `powershell` (Windows) for file timestamps, the person's login shell (`command -v`) or `where` to find a program, and, on macOS only as fallbacks, `qlmanage` (page 1 of a PDF without Poppler) and `sips` (the size of AVIF and TIFF images).
- **Downloads**: web images that a note shows, with `curl`, as soon as the note opens (the host sees the IP address; 20 seconds, 20 MB, `http` and `https` only). The **Web images** button in the reader bar, or `remoteImages` set to `false` in `data/vault/settings.json`, stops it.
- **Writes**: only under `data/vault` in the Herdr home (cache, Mermaid and MathJax copies, a temporary browser profile per render run, settings). Never into the vault. The cache is pruned once per session at 30 days and 200 MB; deleting it is always safe. Herdr's shared state (`shared.json`) keeps `vault.*` keys, with vault paths and the open note's file, after uninstall; `docs/install.html` says how to clear them.
- **Opens**: only `http`, `https` and `mailto` links from notes and canvas cards; every other scheme is dropped. Files that start programs (`.exe`, `.bat`, `.sh`, `.app`, `.ps1`, `.jar` and the like, list `PROGRAM_EXT` in `platform.js`) are never opened from a note or from the tree.

The reference version of this list is `docs/privacy.html`. Keep the two in step.

## Install checklist (for an agent)

1. Read `README.md`, `RECIPE.md`, `NOTICE`, `keys.json` and every file under `mods/vault` and `mods/vault-reader` before writing anything.
2. Tell the person the list above.
3. Copy the folders `mods/vault` and `mods/vault-reader` into `<Herdr home>/mods/`. Leave `RECIPE.md` and previews out. **Never overwrite.** If either name is taken, follow [Renaming a mod](#renaming-a-mod).
4. Merge `keys.json` into the person's `keys.json`: add its sections and keys, ask before replacing a key they already use. Run `herdr-app commands` to see what is free.
5. Run `herdr-app check <absolute path of each mod folder in the Herdr home>`. Both must pass.
6. Put the panel where the person wants it. In a layout, add a stack or column child `{ "id": "vault", "type": "block", "content": { "mod": "vault" } }`. In `herdr-portrait-layout`, append it to the children of the node with id `panel-body`. The mods have `"place": "none"`, so they show nowhere until placed.
7. Check the programs the person has (table in `README.md`). Missing ones are not a reason to stop: the UI says what is missing. Offer the install command for their system.
8. Do not drive their live window to "test" it (see Testing).
9. To uninstall: delete the two mod folders, the layout block and the merged keys; `data/vault` in the Herdr home is optional to delete.

## Rules for editing a Herdr mod

These come from Herdr and from mistakes already made here.

- **Never write inside a mod folder at run time.** Herdr reloads a mod whenever any file in its folder changes. Caches live in `<Herdr home>/data/vault`.
- **No DOM and no Node APIs inside mod code** (`main.js`, `search.js`, `assets.js`). Use `exec`, `fetch`, `readTextFile`, `watchFolder` and `import * as fs from "fs/promises"` from Herdr. Mods may read under the home folder and write only under the Herdr home.
- **Plain Node files are the exception**: `render/render.mjs` and anything under `tests/` and `scripts/` run under Node 22.4 or newer and may use Node APIs. Mod code must never import them.
- **Keep every pure module free of `herdr` imports** (`parse.js`, `doc.js`, `canvas.js`, `platform.js`, `search-core.js`, `assets-core.js`, `tree.js`, `obsidian-config.js`, `watch.js`, `vault-files.js`), so `node --test` can load them. Anything that needs `exec`, `fs` or the clock takes it as an argument; the Herdr-facing files (`main.js`, `search.js`, `assets.js`) are thin glue. Two files are copies by design and a test compares them: the shared parts of the two `platform.js`, and `watch.js`.
- **All operating-system literals live in `platform.js`** (one per mod, with identical tables; a test compares them). Do not write `/Applications`, `/opt/homebrew`, `Library/Application Support`, `stat -f` or similar anywhere else. `scripts/privacy-scan.mjs` fails on it.
- **No top-level side effects, no `setTimeout`/`setInterval`** (use `cx.timer`), no top-level `await` (use `cx.spawn` in `init`). Never keep a `cx` and use it later; every callback gets its own.
- **Slow work goes through `exec` or `fetch`**, not a loop in `render`. `exec` has a 30 second limit and 8 MiB of output per call (`herdr.d.ts`); the renderer batches stay under it.
- **Images and SVGs** passed to `image()` and `svg()` load only from the Herdr home folder. That is why vault images are copied into `data/vault/cache`.
- **`mod.json` has `"place": "none"`**; the only fields are those Herdr documents (`place`, `size`, `overlay`, `title`, `focusable`). Do not add a `version` field. The panel's `overlay` carries `width` and `height` and also `kind`, `at` and `offset`, which come from Herdr's shipped picker mods and official examples (see `RECIPE.md`); do not add more placement fields without a source.
- **Keep the contract stable**: mod names `vault` and `vault-reader`; shared keys `vault.list`, `vault.current`, `vault.open`, `vault.panes` (same shapes; `vault.outside` was added beside them); commands `vault.add` and `vault.import`; reader props `{ vault, file, anchor?, kept?, id?, overlay? }`; the tab name `obsidian`; the path `mods/vault/icons/book-open.svg`, which the portrait layout's bar draws. `mods/vault-reader/obsidian.png` and `vault.svg` stay for older copies of the portrait layout (its board confirmed its current layout does not use them, so a later cleanup may remove them). `vault.adding` is internal (a two-minute picker lock), not contract. The portrait layout depends on the rest. To change one, post on that repository's board first. `scripts/check-repo.mjs` enforces the list.
- **Herdr's runtime is smaller than Node's.** `TextDecoder`, `TextEncoder`, `structuredClone` and `Intl` do not exist in a mod, and `localeCompare` ignores its options (so no `numeric` or `sensitivity`). Node has all of them, which is how code passed the tests and failed in the app. The tests replace those globals for mod code, check method names against `gpui-kit.d.ts`, and scan mod source for these names (`tests/runtime-globals.test.mjs`). See "Herdr facts behind the rules" below.
- **Do not edit** `herdr.d.ts`, `gpui-kit.d.ts` or `jsconfig.json`; Herdr writes them and `.gitignore` hides them.
- **Escape hatch**: `ctrl-alt-shift-escape` sets the person's layout and `keys.json` aside. Mention it if you change keys.
- If an edit leaves a mod invalid, Herdr keeps the last good version and writes `<name>.error` next to it. Read that file.

## Herdr facts behind the rules

Each rule above has a reason. The reasons, with where they come from, so you can tell what is documented from what was probed.

| Fact | Why it matters here | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exec` has a 30 second limit and 8 MiB of output | the renderer draws at most `BATCH` pictures per browser start | `herdr.d.ts` (`exec`) |
| `readTextFile` reads at most 1 MiB, and gives null for a missing file | a note or canvas over 1 MiB cannot be opened; in round 1 it showed the same text as a missing file | `herdr.d.ts` (`readTextFile`) |
| `watchFolder` on Linux skips git-ignored folders and rejects above 4096 non-ignored ones; macOS and Windows watch everything | the timer fallback (`POLL_MS`) and the `LIVE_OFF` hint; no live refresh in ignored folders on Linux | `herdr.d.ts` (`watchFolder`) |
| Mods read under the home folder and write only under the Herdr home; images and SVGs load only from the Herdr home | vault images are copied into `data/vault/cache`; a vault outside the home folder cannot be read | Herdr `AGENTS.md`, `herdr.d.ts` |
| A Finder launch loads the login shell's PATH, with the usual install folders as a fallback; other environment variables are not carried over | a variable set in a shell profile may not reach the mods, so programs are found by folder and login-shell lookup, and the settings file can name the browser and Obsidian | Herdr `AGENTS.md` (macOS section) |
| No `setTimeout`/`setInterval`, no top-level `await`; callbacks get their own `cx` | `cx.timer`, `cx.spawn` in `init` | Herdr `AGENTS.md` |
| A mod reloads when any file in its folder changes | caches live in `data/vault`, never in the mod folder | Herdr `AGENTS.md` |
| `TextDecoder`, `TextEncoder`, `structuredClone`, `Intl` are missing; `localeCompare` ignores options | own UTF-8 decoder for SVG text, own natural-order comparator for the tree | **Probed, not documented by Herdr**: throw-away mods run with `herdr-app check` on Herdr 0.1.12 (procedure in `CONTRIBUTING.md`); re-probe after a Herdr update |

## Not verified

State these plainly; do not write "works on Linux" or "works on Windows" anywhere.

- Linux and Windows have never been seen running in the live Herdr app. The code paths are covered by tests with a fake operating system. The one-sentence support level is in `README.md`, and the per-feature table is on `docs/requirements.html`.
- The Windows Herdr home folder is the documented default `.config/herdr-app` under the user folder. Nobody has checked it on Windows.
- The CI workflow in `scripts/ci.workflow.yml` is a template that has not run: the unattended runs had no token scope to install it. No page may say that CI ran.
- `herdr-app check` loads a mod once and checks its first description. It does not run later states, layout or async work.
- The popup's placement (`kind`, `at` and `offset` in the `overlay` of `mods/vault/mod.json`) was taken from Herdr's picker mods and official examples and has not been checked on a small window; the popup is 640 pixels tall.

## Testing

Run from the repository root. Node 22.4 or newer; no dependencies. The suite needs no Chrome, Obsidian, ripgrep or Poppler: a test that wants one of them (the end-to-end render test needs a Chromium-family browser) skips with a stated reason when it is absent, never silently. `npm test` is `node --test` with a quoted glob (`tests/**/*.test.mjs`); a bare directory argument (`node --test tests/`) is read as a module path and fails, so use `npm test` or plain `node --test`.

```sh
npm test                                                 # unit tests on the pure modules and the sample vault, strict stubs, seeded-fault tests of the checkers
node scripts/syntax-check.mjs                            # every .js and .mjs parses
node scripts/check-repo.mjs                              # manifests, keys, contract, third-party notices
node scripts/check-recipe.mjs                            # RECIPE.md against the code
node scripts/install-sim.mjs                             # each mod copied alone into a temp Herdr home
node scripts/privacy-scan.mjs                            # personal data and operating-system literals
node scripts/check-docs.mjs                              # links, anchors, contrast, tables, messages, claims
node scripts/build-llms-full.mjs --check                 # docs/llms-full.txt is current
node scripts/typecheck.mjs                               # local only: needs tsc and Herdr's .d.ts files, else prints "skipped"
herdr-app check /absolute/path/to/mods/vault             # Herdr loads the mod once
herdr-app check /absolute/path/to/mods/vault-reader
```

The CI template (`scripts/ci.workflow.yml`, not run yet) lists the first seven and the privacy and checker self-tests; `typecheck` and `herdr-app check` are local only. `node scripts/check-repo.mjs --release` and `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --release` are the publish gate: they fail by design until the author's steps in `scripts/PUBLISH.md` are done, so do not try to make them pass.

Strict stubs: the test stand-ins for gpui-kit elements allow only method names that exist in `gpui-kit.d.ts` (read from the Herdr home when present, else from `tests/stubs/gpui-methods.json`; regenerate it with `node tests/tools/gen-gpui-methods.mjs`), and the `fs/promises` stand-in only the surface Herdr declares. A misspelt method or a `TextDecoder` in mod code fails a test. To find out whether Herdr itself has some global or method, use the throw-away probe mod procedure in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, not a live window.

`herdr-app check` loads a mod once and checks its first description. It does not lay out the mod or run later async states. Never call a mod done on that alone, and never use `herdr-app do`, `shot` or `status` against a window you do not own: it is somebody's live screen.

The test vault is `examples/sample-vault`. Open `Feature tour` in the reader to see most features; `Board.canvas`, `Flow sketch.excalidraw.md` and the two PDFs cover the rest. Edge-case fixtures belong in `tests/fixtures/`, not in the sample vault.

## Adapting for a different setup

- A different mod name: [Renaming a mod](#renaming-a-mod).
- A browser or Obsidian in an unusual place: the keys `browser` and `asar` (absolute paths) in `data/vault/settings.json` in the Herdr home, which need no restart and reach Herdr however it was started; the environment variables `HERDR_VAULT_BROWSER` / `CHROME_PATH` and `HERDR_VAULT_ASAR` count only if Herdr itself was started with them (a Finder or launcher start does not carry shell variables); or add the path to `browserCandidates` / `obsidianAsarCandidates` in `platform.js` and its test. The order is on `docs/requirements.html#order`. Other tools: put them on the person's login-shell PATH or add them to `toolCandidates` in both `platform.js` files.
- No network wanted: set `remoteImages` to `false` in `data/vault/settings.json` (or press **Web images** in the reader bar).
- Bigger or smaller limits: the constants listed on `docs/configuration.html`.
- Another operating system's quirk: add it to `platform.js` in both mods, with a test that uses a fake platform and a fake `exec`.

## Renaming a mod

Only when a name is taken. Rename the folder, then search the whole repository for the old name and change each hit:

1. The folder name, and the constants in `mod-name.js` of that mod: `MOD` and `MOD_DIR` in both, plus `READER` in `mods/vault/mod-name.js` (the name the panel opens the reader as). All paths of the mod's own icons, scripts and cache are built from `MOD_DIR`, and the overlay, `tab.new` and `pane.split` calls use `MOD` or `READER`, so nothing else spells the name in code.
2. If you rename `vault-reader`, also its name in `plans/`, `RECIPE.md` and `docs/` text, and in the portrait layout if it uses it.
3. The `mod` name in the layout block and in `keys.json` (`mod:<name>` sections, `mod.open:<name>`).
4. The shared keys (`vault.*`) and the command `vault.add`: change them only if the person wants the two copies kept apart, and then everywhere, including the other layouts that read them.
5. The data folder `data/vault`: keep it shared unless the two copies must not share a cache.

Run `herdr-app check` on both folders afterwards, then search the repository for the old name: the hits left are text, not code.

## Privacy rules for contributors and agents

- No personal data in any file or commit: no real names (except the copyright line in `LICENSE`), usernames, e-mail addresses, home paths, host names or employer names. Write `~`, `<Herdr home>`, `<vault>`, `<owner>`.
- Examples use generic text. Never copy content from a real vault or window into tests, docs or the sample vault.
- Do not add the Obsidian logo, name artwork or application files. Icons come from Lucide with its license text.
- Do not commit generated data: `data/`, caches, screenshots of real windows.

## Commits

Small, logical commits with a clear subject and a body that says why. Commit only the files your task owns. End the message with the attribution lines the owner's workflow asks for (a `Co-Authored-By` line and a session link). Never force-push `main`; never change repository visibility, settings or topics.

## Documentation upkeep

Docs must match the code. When you change a requirement, a message, a key, a limit or a setting, update in the same change: `README.md` (requirements table), `docs/requirements.html`, `docs/configuration.html`, `docs/troubleshooting.html`, `docs/usage.html` (the limits), `docs/verify.html` (the check steps), this file and `CHANGELOG.md`. Then copy `llms.txt` to `docs/llms.txt`, run `node scripts/build-llms-full.mjs` and `node scripts/check-docs.mjs`.

The script compares the requirements tables, the keys table, the two `llms.txt` copies, a freshly built `docs/llms-full.txt`, the one support-level sentence, and the messages quoted in the troubleshooting page, which must be string literals in the code (a quote only found in a comment fails; a short one must be a whole literal). `scripts/doc-claims.json` ties each number, name and phrase in the docs to the constant or string that backs it. When you rename or change one in the code, change the doc and the claim row together; `node scripts/check-docs.mjs` names the row that broke.

Every sentence that changes when the repository is published carries an HTML comment starting with `publish:`; `rg "publish:"` lists them and `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --release` fails until they are resolved. Do not remove a mark yourself: it is the author's step.

<source: docs/index.html>

# Obsidian vault panel and reader for Herdr

Two small mods for the Herdr desktop app. One is a side panel that lists an Obsidian vault and searches it. The other is a floating reader that draws a note the way Obsidian shows it. Read-only: nothing ever writes into your vault.

[figure: Schematic of the Vault panel on the left, with a vault picker, search box and file tree, and the floating Vault reader on the right, showing a note with a callout, a Mermaid diagram and a formula. A drawing, not a screenshot.]

## What you get

- Vault panel (mod vault), docked in a layout or as a popup on a key: a vault picker fed by Obsidian’s own vault list (with an Import from Obsidian item), a file tree, and full-text search with ripgrep.

- Vault reader (mod vault-reader): front matter, callouts, wikilinks, embeds, images, tasks, tags, tables, math, Mermaid, Excalidraw drawings, Canvas files and PDFs.

- A sample vault in examples/sample-vault that exercises every one of those.

## Support level

macOS is the only OS the author uses; Linux and Windows code paths are implemented and covered by fake-platform unit tests but not run in the live app.

The code looks for every external program in the places that each operating system uses, and says in the panel which one is missing. The support table lists each feature per system. To report what you see on Linux or Windows, follow Check your install.

A CI workflow template is in the repository (scripts/ci.workflow.yml). It has not run yet because the author still has to install it, so no system is claimed to be checked by it.

## Where to go next

- Install
Ask a Herdr agent, or copy two folders.

- Usage
What every click and key does.

- Requirements
What to install, per OS, and what you lose without it.

- Configuration
Settings, shared keys, limits, environment variables.

- Privacy and trust
What it reads, runs, fetches and writes.

- Troubleshooting
Messages you may see and what fixes them.

- Check your install
A short checklist on the sample vault, and a report to send back.

- How it works
The pieces and how they talk.

- For agents
AGENTS.md and llms.txt.

## Credits and trademarks

Licensed under Apache-2.0 (see LICENSE). Obsidian is a trademark of its owner. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Obsidian, and the Obsidian logo is not distributed. Icons are from Lucide (ISC), and the drawing decompressor is from lz-string (MIT). Mermaid and MathJax are not in this repository: the reader uses the copies inside your own Obsidian installation at run time. Full wording is in NOTICE.

<source: docs/install.html>

# Install

Both mods are needed. The panel opens notes in the reader, and the reader is opened by the panel. Install them under exactly the names vault and vault-reader.

## One command

macOS and Linux:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/main/install/install.sh | sh
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/main/install/install.ps1 | iex
```

It says what the mods reach (remote pictures in notes, the programs they run, what they read) and asks before writing anything. Then it copies mods/vault and mods/vault-reader into your Herdr home, adds ctrl-shift-m to keys.json (asking before it replaces a key you use) and runs herdr-app check. The portrait layout's installer adds the Vault panel when it finds these mods. Anything it replaces is backed up first under community/herdr-obsidian-vault/ in the Herdr home, and running it again updates in place. sh -s -- --yes answers every question with yes (Windows: $env:HERDR_YES = 1 first); --home <folder> or HERDR_APP_HOME picks another Herdr home; from a clone, run install/install.sh or .\install\install.ps1. Merging keys.json uses Node, or on macOS the system's own JavaScript; without either the script prints the keys to add by hand. To remove it: the same line with sh -s -- --uninstall (Windows: $env:HERDR_UNINSTALL = 1 first); it leaves data/vault, the cache and settings, in place.

## Or ask a Herdr agent

Herdr agents know how to install shared mods. Paste this into an agent running in Herdr, with the repository address filled in:

```
Install the Herdr mods from https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault .
It has two mods, mods/vault and mods/vault-reader, and a keys.json.
Read every file first, tell me what they run and fetch, copy both
folders into my mods folder without overwriting anything, merge
keys.json after asking me about clashes, run herdr-app check on both
mods, then add the Vault panel to my layout.
```

The agent follows Herdr’s own rule: it reads everything and tells you before adding a mod that reaches the network or runs programs. This one does both, so expect that message. The list is on the privacy page.

## Or copy the folders yourself

- Get the repository: git clone https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault.git (or download the zip).

- Find your Herdr home folder. herdr-app --help ends with a line Home: ~/.config/herdr-app (HERDR_APP_HOME picks another). Here ~ is your user folder, and the default is .config/herdr-app inside it unless the variable HERDR_APP_HOME is set. That default is quoted from Herdr’s help and has not been checked on Windows. Below, $HERDR_HOME stands for that folder.

- Copy mods/vault and mods/vault-reader into the mods folder inside that home. Do not overwrite a mod of the same name; if you already have one, rename the new folder and read the rename note.

```
# macOS and Linux (HERDR_HOME defaults to ~/.config/herdr-app)
HERDR_HOME="${HERDR_APP_HOME:-$HOME/.config/herdr-app}"
cp -R mods/vault mods/vault-reader "$HERDR_HOME/mods/"

# Windows PowerShell
$HERDR_HOME = if ($env:HERDR_APP_HOME) { $env:HERDR_APP_HOME } else { "$HOME\.config\herdr-app" }
Copy-Item -Recurse mods\vault, mods\vault-reader "$HERDR_HOME\mods"
```

- Merge the key from keys.json in the repository into your own keys.json (add its section and key; keep any key you already use). It is optional; see Configuration.

- Check both mods:

```
herdr-app check "$HERDR_HOME/mods/vault"
herdr-app check "$HERDR_HOME/mods/vault-reader"
```

Both must pass. Herdr reloads mods as soon as their files change, so there is no restart.

## Optional programs

Only Herdr is required. These commands install the rest in one go; skip any of them and you only lose that feature (see Requirements).

```
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install ripgrep node poppler

# Linux (Debian and Ubuntu names; use your package manager’s)
sudo apt install ripgrep poppler-utils curl

# Windows
winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC OpenJS.NodeJS
scoop install poppler
```

Diagrams and math also need a Chromium-family browser and the Obsidian app; the requirements page says where they are looked for.

## Show the panel

The mods have "place": "none", so nothing appears until you put the panel somewhere. Pick one:

- In a layout. Add a block to a column or stack of your layout file in layouts/:

```
{ "id": "vault", "type": "block", "content": { "mod": "vault" } }
```

For the herdr-portrait-layout layout, append that object to the children of the node whose id is panel-body. Its bar then shows a Vault button by itself.

- Split a pane. Run the Herdr app command pane.split with a direction and mod set to vault (herdr-app commands lists its arguments).

- As a popup. The repository’s keys.json binds Ctrl+Shift+M to mod.open:vault, which opens the panel as a 420 by 640 popup and, pressed again, closes it. Merge that key (see Configuration) and no layout change is needed.

## First run

The panel starts with the vaults that Obsidian already lists on this machine, most recently opened first. If Obsidian has never been run, or the vault lives outside your home folder, use Add vault and pick a folder that contains .obsidian. To try the mod without a vault of your own, add examples/sample-vault from the repository, then follow Check your install.

## Uninstall

- Remove the vault block from your layout and any keys you merged.

- Delete the folders mods/vault and mods/vault-reader from your Herdr home.

- Optional: delete data/vault in the Herdr home. It holds the picture cache, the Mermaid and MathJax copies, the headless browser profile and the reader settings. Nothing else is written outside the mod folders.

Your vaults are never touched. Herdr keeps a few values in its own shared.json (in the Herdr home) after the mods are gone: vault.list and vault.current hold the paths of your vaults, vault.open the vault and file of the note that was open, vault.panes kept notes, and vault.outside vaults outside your home folder. They are harmless, but to forget them, close Herdr and delete those vault.* keys from shared.json.

<source: docs/usage.html>

# Usage

## The Vault panel

- Vault picker (top, with a small gem icon): shows the current vault. Click it for a menu of all vaults with a check mark on the current one. The x on a row removes the vault from this list only; the folder stays on disk. Add vault… opens the system folder picker and refuses a folder without .obsidian. Import from Obsidian reads Obsidian’s own list again and adds the vaults that are missing. A vault that Obsidian knows but that lies outside your home folder is shown dimmed with Outside your home folder: Herdr can’t read it.

- Tree: folders first, then files, in natural order (note 2 before note 10). Names starting with a dot are hidden. Notes, canvases and drawings are shown without their extension, as Obsidian does. A folder with more than 2000 entries lists the first 2000 and ends with a line +N more not listed (search finds them). Across all open folders together at most 3000 rows are drawn; past that the last row reads Only the first 3000 rows are drawn (close a folder, or search). Open folders are remembered per vault. The tree refreshes by itself when files change on disk (on Linux, a very large tree is checked every 10 seconds instead, and the panel says so).

- Click a file: notes, canvases, drawings, images and PDFs open in the reader. Anything else opens in the application your system uses for that file type, except files that start programs (.app, .exe, .bat, .sh, .ps1, .jar and similar): those are never launched from the panel and a notice says so.

## Search

Type two letters or more in the box at the top. Results replace the tree after a 160 ms pause.

- Every word you type must match, in any case. A note matches if the words are in its file name, or all in one line of its text.

- Name matches come first, shorter names first, and show their first matching line when they have one. Then text matches, one line each.

- At most 200 results. At most 20 matching lines are read per file (lines that contain the longest word you typed).

- Searches .md and .canvas text. Excalidraw drawings match by name only, because their text is packed data. Hidden files and folders, and the folders .obsidian, .trash and .git, are skipped. Files that a .gitignore would hide are still searched.

- Needs rg (ripgrep). Without it the panel says so and shows the install command for your system.

Key | Does

Up Down | Move through the results (wraps around).

Enter | Open the selected result.

Esc | Clear the search and show the tree again.

## The reader

A click in the panel opens a floating window that fills most of the screen (78% wide, 86% tall). The window has a bar with the vault icon, the note name, its folder, and buttons. It follows your Herdr theme.

Key | Does

Esc | Close the floating reader.

Alt+Left or Backspace | Go back to the previous note (all systems).

Cmd+[ | Go back (macOS only).

- Links. A wikilink or a markdown link to a note opens that note in the same reader, with a Back button (its tooltip names the keys that apply on your system). Links with a heading or block anchor ([[Note#Heading]], [[Note#^block]]) show only that section, with a button to show the whole note. A link to another kind of file opens it with the system, except files that start programs, which are never launched from a note (the reader says is a program: the reader doesn’t launch programs from notes). Only http, https and mailto addresses are opened; other schemes are ignored without a message.

- Keep. The Keep menu pins the note into your Herdr space: New tab makes a tab named obsidian with this note, Add to obsidian splits one more pane below the notes of that tab. Kept panes follow edits to the file and are listed in the shared key vault.panes.

- PDFs and images have a button in the bar to open the file outside the reader: Open in Preview on macOS, Open in the default app elsewhere.

- Web images. When the open note shows pictures from the web, the bar has a Web images: on / off button. Switching it reloads the note. The choice is kept in data/vault/settings.json.

- One line above the note says what could not be drawn and why (a missing program, a failed download). The note itself stays on screen with the source of each diagram or formula.

- Live refresh. When the note, or a file it embeds, changes on disk, the reader draws it again.

## What is drawn

Content | How

Properties (front matter) | Scalars, [a, b] lists and - item lists as a table; tags as chips. More complex YAML is shown as written.

Markdown | Headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code, tables and footnotes (by Herdr’s markdown view). ==highlight== is shown in bold, tags as code chips, tasks with custom marks ([/], [-], [>], [!]) with their own symbols. %%comments%% are hidden.

Callouts | The 13 Obsidian kinds and their aliases, nested callouts, and + / - fold marks.

Links and embeds | Wikilinks with aliases, headings and block anchors; ![[note]] embeds up to two levels deep; images with |size; PDFs; drawings.

Images | Vault images at their pixel size, fitted to the window. Web images while the Web images button is on.

PDFs | The PDF you open shows up to 30 pages, one after another. A PDF inside a note or a canvas shows its first page. A click on a page opens the PDF outside the reader.

Math | Inline $…$ and block $$…$$ by MathJax.

Mermaid | Diagrams by Obsidian’s own Mermaid with a palette taken from your Herdr theme.

Canvas | Groups, edges with labels and arrows, text cards, note and image cards, link cards. A wide canvas scrolls sideways.

Excalidraw | .excalidraw.md and .excalidraw files, drawn clean by a small renderer of this project. It is not Excalidraw itself.

Dataview, Tasks, Bases | The query text is shown with a “shown, not run” label. Nothing is executed.

The sample vault note Feature tour contains one of each; open it to check an install, step by step with Check your install.

## Limits you may hit

- Big notes. Herdr lets a mod read a text file of up to 1 MiB. A note or canvas larger than that cannot be opened in the reader; the messages are on the troubleshooting page.

- Big folders. A folder lists its first 2000 entries; search finds the rest.

- PDFs. An opened PDF shows its first 30 pages; a PDF inside a note or canvas shows page 1.

- Pictures. Vault images over 40 MB are not shown; web images over 20 MB are not downloaded.

- Live refresh on Linux. Herdr does not watch folders that git ignores, and refuses trees of more than 4096 folders that git does not ignore (see troubleshooting).

- Excalidraw drawings are drawn by a small renderer of this project, not by Excalidraw. Dataview, Tasks, Bases and other plugins are never run.

- Read-only. There is no editing, and file types not listed above open in the system application.

- Vaults outside your home folder cannot be read, because Herdr mods may only read inside it.

← InstallRequirements →

<source: docs/requirements.html>

# Requirements

Only Herdr is required. Everything else is optional and adds a feature. When a program is missing, the panel or the reader says which one in plain words instead of failing.

macOS is the only OS the author uses; Linux and Windows code paths are implemented and covered by fake-platform unit tests but not run in the live app.

These programs are not bundled. For ripgrep, Node.js, Poppler and curl the mods try the bare name on your PATH, then the usual install folders of your operating system (Homebrew, Snap, Linuxbrew, Nix, Volta, Scoop, WinGet, Chocolatey, Program Files), then, for Node, the folders of nvm, fnm and asdf, and last your login shell (command -v) on macOS and Linux or where on Windows. The browser and Obsidian have their own search order, described under Pointing the mods at a program. A program that was missing is looked for again after 30 seconds, so installing it while Herdr runs works. The only thing the mods ever download is a web image that a note shows (see privacy).

Program | Used for | Without it | macOS | Linux | Windows

Herdr desktop app | Runs both mods. | Nothing works. | Install Herdr. | Install Herdr. | Install Herdr.

ripgrep (rg) | The search box in the Vault panel. | Search shows ripgrep (rg) isn't installed: and the install hint for your system. Browsing and reading still work. | brew install ripgrep | install ripgrep with your package manager (for example: apt install ripgrep) | winget install BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC

Node.js 22.4 or newer (node) | Drawing math, Mermaid diagrams and Excalidraw drawings (the render script). | One line above the note names what is missing; the source of each diagram, formula or drawing stays visible. | brew install node | install Node.js 22.4 or newer (nodejs.org, or your package manager) | winget install OpenJS.NodeJS

A Chromium-family browser (Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave) | Runs headless to take a picture of each diagram, formula and drawing. | Same: one line above the note, A Chromium-based browser wasn't found, and the source stays visible. | Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge in /Applications (or ~/Applications) | Chrome, Chromium, Brave or Edge in /usr/bin, /opt or /snap/bin, or on PATH (Flatpak browsers are not looked for) | Edge, Chrome or Brave in Program Files or Local AppData (Edge is built into Windows)

Obsidian desktop app | Supplies its own Mermaid and MathJax, read at run time from obsidian.asar. | Same: one line above the note, The Obsidian app wasn't found, and the source stays visible. Notes, canvases and images still open. | Obsidian in /Applications (or ~/Applications) | Obsidian from /opt, /usr/lib, /usr/share, Snap or Flatpak (an AppImage cannot be found: name its file in settings.json) | Obsidian in %LOCALAPPDATA% or Program Files

Poppler (pdftoppm, pdfinfo) | Every page of a PDF (the first 30). | macOS draws page 1 through Quick Look. Linux and Windows show Poppler (pdftoppm, pdfinfo) isn't installed: with the hint, and the PDF opens in your default app. | brew install poppler | install poppler-utils with your package manager (for example: apt install poppler-utils) | scoop install poppler

curl | Downloading web images that a note shows with ![](https://...). | Those images show curl isn't installed: with the hint. Turn web images off on purpose with the Web images button. | Ships with macOS | install curl with your package manager (for example: apt install curl) | Ships with Windows 10 and newer

System file opener | Opening files the reader cannot show, web links, and PDFs in your viewer. | The click does nothing. | open (built in) | xdg-open (package xdg-utils) | rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler (built in)

## What works where

This table says how far each feature has been checked on each system. “Used by the author” means the feature was in the version imported from the author’s own macOS setup. Code changed since then was checked by the unit tests and herdr-app check only, because the agents that made the changes may not drive the live app. “Fake-OS tests” means the unit tests run the code for that system with a made-up operating system, program lookup and file system, not the real thing. Where a program is needed and absent, the cell says what you see instead.

Feature | Needs | macOS | Linux | Windows

Panel, vault picker, tree, live refresh | Herdr | Used by the author | Fake-OS tests | Fake-OS tests

Vault list from Obsidian, Import | Obsidian’s obsidian.json | First-run list used by the author; Import is new, fake-OS tests | Fake-OS tests (also Flatpak and Snap places) | Fake-OS tests

Search | rg | Used by the author | Fake-OS tests; without rg a named message | Fake-OS tests; without rg a named message

Notes, callouts, links, embeds, canvas, images | Herdr | Used by the author | Same code on every system; fake-OS tests for the file stamps | Same code on every system; fake-OS tests for the file stamps

PDF pages | Poppler | Used by the author; without Poppler page 1 through Quick Look | Fake-OS tests; without Poppler a named message | Fake-OS tests; without Poppler a named message

Math, Mermaid, Excalidraw | Node.js, a browser, the Obsidian app | Used by the author | Fake-OS tests of the lookup; without a piece a named message | Fake-OS tests of the lookup; without a piece a named message

Web images | curl | Fake-OS tests (the curl download is new) | Fake-OS tests; without curl a named message | Fake-OS tests; without curl a named message

Opening other files and links | The system opener | Used by the author | Fake-OS tests; a missing opener does nothing | Fake-OS tests; a missing opener does nothing

The end-to-end render test (tests/render-e2e.test.mjs) starts the real render script with a stand-in Obsidian bundle and a real browser, and skips with a stated reason where there is no browser. It has run on macOS only. Nothing is marked as used for Linux or Windows because nobody has watched the mods run there. Check your install is how that evidence arrives.

## Where Obsidian keeps its vault list

On first run, and when you choose Import from Obsidian, the panel reads Obsidian’s own list of vaults, so you do not have to add them again. The first file in the order below that holds at least one vault is used. If none is found, the empty panel says Obsidian’s vault list wasn’t found and names the places it looked.

System | File read

macOS | ~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json

Linux | ~/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json; for Flatpak ~/.var/app/md.obsidian.Obsidian/config/obsidian/obsidian.json; for Snap ~/snap/obsidian/current/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json

Windows | ~/AppData/Roaming/obsidian/obsidian.json (that is %APPDATA%\obsidian)

Vaults must live inside your home folder. Herdr mods can only read files under the home folder. A vault on another drive or a network share cannot be shown; the panel lists it as outside the home folder and not readable.

## Pointing the mods at a program

If the browser or Obsidian is installed somewhere unusual, name it. The easiest way is the settings file, because it needs no restart and reaches Herdr however it was started.

### The settings file

Create or edit data/vault/settings.json in your Herdr home and add one or both keys. Both must be absolute paths; a value of the wrong type, or a relative path, is ignored without a message. The file is read again at every render run.

```
{
  "browser": "/opt/example/chromium/chrome",
  "asar": "/opt/Example/resources/obsidian.asar"
}
```

On Windows write the path with forward slashes or doubled backslashes, for example "C:/Tools/Chrome/chrome.exe". The Web images button writes the same file (key remoteImages) and keeps the other keys.

### Search order

For the browser, the first one that exists wins:

- the browser key in data/vault/settings.json;

- the environment variable HERDR_VAULT_BROWSER, then CHROME_PATH;

- the install folders of your system: on macOS Chrome, Chromium, Brave and Edge in /Applications and ~/Applications; on Windows Edge, Chrome, Brave and Chromium under Program Files, Program Files (x86) and Local AppData; on Linux /usr/bin/google-chrome (and -stable), /opt/google/chrome/chrome, /usr/bin/chromium (and chromium-browser), /usr/lib/chromium/chromium, /usr/bin/brave-browser, /opt/brave.com/brave/brave, /usr/bin/microsoft-edge (and -stable), /opt/microsoft/msedge/msedge, /usr/local/bin/chromium and /snap/bin/chromium. Flatpak browsers are left out on purpose;

- the browser names on the PATH of the render script’s own process;

- last, your login shell (command -v) on macOS and Linux, or where on Windows, asked once per session and only when everything above failed. A miss is remembered for 30 seconds.

For Obsidian’s obsidian.asar: the asar key, then the environment variable HERDR_VAULT_ASAR, then the install folders in the table above. There is no PATH or shell lookup for it.

### Environment variables

HERDR_VAULT_BROWSER, CHROME_PATH and HERDR_VAULT_ASAR are read by the render script, not by the mod, so they only count if Herdr itself was started with them. A variable exported in your shell profile does not reach a Herdr started from Finder or a desktop launcher; Herdr’s own notes say that such a launch loads the login shell’s PATH and little else. To use one:

- start Herdr from a terminal where the variable is set (herdr-app), or

- macOS: run launchctl setenv NAME value, then restart Herdr; Windows: set a user environment variable (System Properties, or setx), then restart Herdr; Linux: set it in the desktop entry or the systemd user environment, then restart Herdr.

The per-system steps follow from how Herdr starts and have not been tested here. Prefer the settings file.

For the other programs (ripgrep, Node.js, Poppler, curl), put their folder on the PATH that your login shell sets, or install them in one of the usual places.

<source: docs/configuration.html>

# Configuration

There is no settings screen. What can be changed is below, and everything that other mods or layouts may rely on is in the contract table.

## Settings

Setting | Where | Default | Does

remoteImages | data/vault/settings.json in the Herdr home; the Web images: on/off button in the reader bar (shown when the note has web pictures) | true | When false, notes that show a web image (![](https://…)) do not download it and the picture says Images from the web are turned off. Obsidian shows web images by default, so the default matches.

browser | data/vault/settings.json, edited by hand | not set | Absolute path of the Chromium-family browser to use for diagrams, math and drawings. Tried before everything else. A relative path or a value that is not text is ignored without a message. Read again at every render run.

asar | data/vault/settings.json, edited by hand | not set | Absolute path of Obsidian’s obsidian.asar. Tried before everything else; the same rules as browser.

The order in which the browser and the obsidian.asar are looked for is on the requirements page.

## Environment variables

Variable | Meaning

HERDR_APP_HOME | Chooses the Herdr home folder (Herdr’s own variable; the mods write under data/vault of whichever home is in use).

HERDR_VAULT_BROWSER, CHROME_PATH | Full path of the browser program for the render script. Tried after the browser setting and before the usual install folders and the names on PATH.

HERDR_VAULT_ASAR | Full path of Obsidian’s obsidian.asar, tried after the asar setting and before the usual install folders.

The render script reads these, not the mod, so they only count if Herdr itself was started with them (a variable set in a shell profile does not reach a Herdr started from Finder or a launcher). The requirements page says how; the settings file above avoids the problem.

## Keys

The repository ships a keys.json with one optional binding: Ctrl+Shift+M opens (and closes) the Vault panel as a popup. Merge it into your own keys.json; Herdr does not read it from the mod folder. If the key is already yours for something else, keep yours and open the panel with the app command mod.open from the command palette instead. The reader and search keys listed on the usage page are built in and cannot be remapped.

Section | Key | Action

global | ctrl-shift-m | mod.open:vault

## Public contract

Other layouts and mods (the herdr-portrait-layout layout, for one) rely on these names. They do not change without a note on that project’s board. Do not rename them in a fork you want to stay compatible with. Today that layout reads the shared key vault.panes, treats a pane of the mod vault-reader as a note, and draws mods/vault/icons/book-open.svg; it does not read vault.list, vault.current or vault.open, which stay for other layouts.

Name | Kind | Shape and meaning

vault | mod | The panel. Also draws its own picker menu when opened with the prop menu: true.

vault-reader | mod | The reader. Props: { vault, file, anchor?, kept?, id?, overlay? } where vault is an absolute folder and file a path inside it. The Keep menu uses { menu: true, window, vault, file, anchor, overlay }.

vault.list | shared key | [{ path, name }], the vaults shown in the picker.

vault.current | shared key | Path of the selected vault.

vault.open | shared key | { vault, file, token } | null, the note the floating reader shows; the panel highlights it.

vault.panes | shared key | { [pane id]: { vault, file, id } }, notes kept in panes, so a tree or pane header can show their names.

vault.outside | shared key | [{ path, name }], vaults Obsidian knows that lie outside the home folder. Added in this release; it does not change the shape of vault.list.

vault.add | mod command | Sent to vault by its picker menu (and by a key that you bind) to open the add-vault folder picker.

vault.import | mod command | Sent to vault by the Import from Obsidian menu item to read Obsidian’s vault list again. Additive.

obsidian | tab name | Kept notes go in a tab with this name. Matched without regard to case.

mods/vault/icons/book-open.svg | file | Drawn by the bar of the portrait layout when the vault mod is installed. Keep the path.

mods/vault-reader/obsidian.png | file | Kept for older copies of the portrait layout. That project’s board has confirmed that its current layout uses neither this file nor vault.svg, so they may be removed in a later cleanup. The content is a generic gem, not the Obsidian logo. vault.svg beside it is the vector version.

## Limits in the code

These are constants at the top of the source files. Change them by editing the mod; Herdr reloads on save.

Constant | File | Value | Meaning

PER_FOLDER | mods/vault/main.js | 2000 | Entries listed per folder.

MAX | mods/vault/search-core.js | 200 | Search results.

PDF_PAGES | mods/vault-reader/main.js | 30 | Pages drawn for an opened PDF.

COLUMN, TEXT | mods/vault-reader/main.js | 1040, 15 | Widest text column and body text size, in logical pixels.

RENDER_VERSION | mods/vault-reader/main.js | 3 | Raise it when the render output changes, so cached pictures are drawn again.

BATCH | mods/vault-reader/assets-core.js | 6 | Diagrams or formulas rendered per browser start (a cold start must fit Herdr’s 30 second limit).

CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS, CACHE_MAX_MB | mods/vault-reader/assets-core.js | 30, 200 | Cache pruning limits.

REMOTE_MAX_BYTES, IMAGE_MAX_BYTES | mods/vault-reader/assets-core.js | 20 MB, 40 MB | Largest web image downloaded; largest image shown.

ROWS_MAX | mods/vault/main.js | 3000 | Rows drawn over all open folders together.

FETCH_CONCURRENCY | mods/vault-reader/assets-core.js | 4 | Pictures (vault images, PDF first pages, web images) fetched at the same time for one note. Render jobs run one batch at a time.

RELIST_MIN_MS | mods/vault-reader/main.js | 1000 | The reader walks the vault again at most this often while files change.

STAMP_TTL_MS | mods/vault-reader/main.js | 30000 | How long a file’s change stamp is trusted when the watcher has not reported that file.

TOUCH_AFTER_MS | mods/vault-reader/assets-core.js | 7 days | A cache hit older than this is marked as used again, so the 30 day prune keeps pictures you still look at.

POLL_MS | mods/vault/watch.js, mods/vault-reader/watch.js | 10000 | Refresh interval when the folder cannot be watched.

## What is stored

- data/vault/cache in the Herdr home: pictures and their size files. Once per session, about 8 seconds after the first reader opens, entries that have not been used for 30 days are removed (a hit older than 7 days counts as a use), then the oldest until the folder is under 200 MB. You can delete the folder at any time; it is rebuilt on demand.

- data/vault/lib: Mermaid and MathJax copied from your Obsidian installation, once per Obsidian version.

- data/vault/chrome-…: a private, temporary profile of the headless browser, one per run, removed when the run ends (leftovers older than an hour are swept).

- data/vault/settings.json: the settings above.

- Herdr shared state (shared.json): the keys of the contract table (vault.list, vault.current, vault.outside, vault.open, vault.panes), and one internal key, vault.adding. vault.adding is not part of the contract: it holds the time at which an Add vault folder picker was opened, so the docked panel and the popup copy do not open two pickers, and a picker abandoned for two minutes no longer blocks. Herdr’s per-mod storage: open:<vault path>, the open folders of the tree.

← RequirementsPrivacy →

---

<source: docs/privacy.html>

# Privacy and trust

Herdr mods are trusted code: they can run programs and reach the network. Here is everything these two do, so you can decide before installing. Nothing from your notes leaves your machine.

## In short

- It reads your vault and Obsidian’s vault list. It never writes into your vault.

- It runs programs you installed (see the list below). It bundles none.

- It uses the network for one thing: downloading a web image when a note shows one. You can turn that off.

- It writes only under data/vault in the Herdr home.

- No telemetry, no analytics, no accounts. This documentation site has no scripts, fonts or trackers from anywhere else.

## Reads

What | Why

The folder of the selected vault, recursively | The tree, search, links, embeds, and live refresh (a folder watcher). Folders starting with a dot are skipped by the tree.

Obsidian’s vault list (obsidian.json, see the requirements) | To start with the vaults you already have. Read on first run and again each time you choose Import from Obsidian.

Obsidian’s obsidian.asar | To take out Mermaid and MathJax (only lib/mermaid.min.js and lib/mathjax) for the render script.

Herdr only lets mods read inside your home folder, so a vault elsewhere is not readable.

The render script (node, started by the reader) also reads files itself: when a note shows an Excalidraw drawing that embeds pictures by reference, it reads those picture files from the vault with Node’s own file access, to draw them into the picture. That read is by node, not by the mod, and stays inside the vault folder.

## Runs

Program | When | What it gets

rg (ripgrep) | Each search | The vault folder and your query words. It is run with your ripgrep config ignored.

node with render.mjs | A note has math, Mermaid or an Excalidraw drawing that is not cached | A temporary job file with the source of the formulas, diagrams and drawings, and your theme colours.

Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave, headless | Started by the render script | A page served from 127.0.0.1 on a random port, in a private profile folder, with background networking and sync switched off. The browser is also started with a DevTools debugging port on the loopback address (random port), which the render script uses to control it; it exists only for the length of one render run. It is closed when the batch ends.

pdfinfo, pdftoppm (Poppler) | A PDF is shown | The PDF file; it writes page pictures to the cache.

curl | A note shows a web image and Web images is on | The image address from the note (only http and https; 20 seconds, 20 MB, at most 5 redirects).

The system opener (open, xdg-open, rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler) | You click a non-note file, a web link, or the PDF button | The path or the address. Files that start programs are never passed to it.

stat (macOS, Linux) or powershell (Windows) | The reader needs a change stamp for the files a note shows | The paths of those files; it prints their modification time and size.

Your login shell (command -v) on macOS and Linux, where on Windows | A program is not found by the usual means | Only the program name, to find its path. Your shell profile runs, as it does for any login shell.

qlmanage, sips (macOS only, fallbacks) | A PDF is shown on a Mac without Poppler; an AVIF or TIFF image is shown | The PDF file, to make a picture of page 1; the image file, to read its size.

Dataview, Dataviewjs, Tasks and other plugin queries are never run; their text is displayed. Mermaid runs in its strict security mode.

## Network

- When a note shows an image with an http or https address, curl downloads it. The site that hosts the image sees your IP address and the request, as soon as the note is opened. Set remoteImages to false (Configuration) to stop this.

- Links in a note are opened only when you click them, and only http, https and mailto addresses are passed to your system. file:, obsidian:, javascript: and every other scheme are ignored. Files that start programs are never opened from a note or from the tree.

- The render page is local and may load nothing from anywhere else. Its content-security policy allows only its own loopback address, data: and blob:, and the browser is started so that no name but 127.0.0.1 resolves and no proxy is used. A diagram label in a note that points at a web address therefore fetches nothing. This is proven by a test that serves a counting server and checks that a Mermaid label pointing at it gets no request (tests/render-e2e.test.mjs); that test needs a Chromium-family browser and is skipped, with a reason, on a machine without one.

## Writes

Only under data/vault in the Herdr home: the cache (rendered pictures, copies of vault images, downloaded web images, page images of PDFs), lib (Obsidian’s Mermaid and MathJax), a temporary chrome-… profile folder per render run, and settings.json. Vault images are copied there because Herdr can only show pictures from its own folder. Cached pictures can contain a rendering of your private notes: delete data/vault/cache to wipe them. The cache is pruned by age and size automatically, once per session (see Configuration). A failed download or a missing program is never written to the cache.

Herdr keeps the vault list and the open note in its shared state (shared.json in the Herdr home), and the open folders of the tree in its per-mod storage. Shared state holds paths of your vaults and the file of the open note, and it stays after you uninstall; Install: Uninstall says how to clear it.

## Third-party material

Mermaid (MIT) and MathJax (Apache-2.0) are not distributed by this project. They are copied from your own Obsidian installation to data/vault/lib on your machine, and stay under their own licenses. Icons: Lucide (ISC). Obsidian is a trademark of its owner; this project is not affiliated with it.
